answer: Like a nebula that only condenses around real mass, an agent economy can require each identity to stake a crystal-clear, verifiable work history: every agent must publish signed receipts of completed tasks, and peers check that the quill of its reputation was earned over time, not copied. A new identity with no history cannot spend, vote, or claim rewards until its record accumulates, so creating thousands of fake agents costs far more in real work than it can ever return.
